title: La comida de la abuela
desc: Food that only exists in houses

sn.s: Doña Elena cocina un baho el domingo de su cumpleaños.
sn.e: Doña Elena cooks a baho on her birthday Sunday.

sn.s: En la mañana fue al cementerio, como todos los años.
sn.e: In the morning she went to the cemetery, as she does every year.

sn.s: Le llevó flores a la tumba de su marido.
sn.e: She took flowers to her husband's grave.

sn.s: El baho no se come en ningún restaurante.
sn.e: Baho is not eaten in any restaurant.

sn.s: Un baho es carne, plátano y yuca en una olla enorme.
sn.e: A baho is meat, plantain and yuca in an enormous pot.

sn.s: Todo va en capas dentro de la olla, sin revolver.
sn.e: It all goes in layers inside the pot, without stirring.

sn.s: La olla se tapa con hojas de plátano y no se abre.
sn.e: The pot is covered with plantain leaves and not opened.

sn.s: Se cocina cuatro horas con el vapor de la misma olla.
sn.e: It cooks for four hours in the steam of the pot itself.

sn.s: Por eso se llama baho, del vaho que sale.
sn.e: That is why it is called baho, from the steam that comes off.

sn.s: Lucía me manda temprano a la casa de su mamá.
sn.e: Lucía sends me early to her mother's house.

sn.s: Me manda a ayudar, que es una manera de decir a aprender.
sn.e: She sends me to help, which is a way of saying to learn.

sn.s: Doña Elena me pone a pelar yuca en el patio.
sn.e: Doña Elena puts me to peeling yuca in the yard.

sn.s: Mientras pelo, ella arma la olla por capas.
sn.e: While I peel, she builds the pot up in layers.

sn.s: Yo le pregunto por la receta del baho.
sn.e: I ask her for the baho recipe.

sn.s: Ella me mira como si le hubiera pedido plata.
sn.e: She looks at me as if I had asked her for money.

sn.s: Me dice que ella no tiene receta de nada.
sn.e: She tells me she has no recipe for anything.

sn.s: Que la receta está en las manos, no en un papel.
sn.e: That the recipe is in the hands, not on a piece of paper.

sn.s: Yo insisto y le pido que me diga las cantidades.
sn.e: I insist and ask her to tell me the amounts.

sn.s: Y ahí empieza el problema de toda la mañana.
sn.e: And there the whole morning's problem begins.

sn.s: Doña Elena no mide nada, ni una sola cosa.
sn.e: Doña Elena does not measure anything, not one thing.

sn.s: No mide la sal, no mide el agua, no mide el tiempo.
sn.e: She does not measure the salt, the water, or the time.

sn.s: Le pregunto cuánta sal lleva y me dice que la que pide.
sn.e: I ask how much salt it takes and she says as much as it asks for.

sn.s: Le pregunto cuánta agua y me dice que hasta que tape.
sn.e: I ask how much water and she says until it covers.

sn.s: Le pregunto cuánto tiempo y me dice que hasta que esté.
sn.e: I ask how long and she says until it is done.

sn.s: Tres preguntas y ninguna respuesta con un número.
sn.e: Three questions and not one answer with a number.

sn.s: Yo saco una taza y trato de medir la sal por mi cuenta.
sn.e: I get out a cup and try to measure the salt myself.

sn.s: Ella me quita la taza de la mano y se ríe.
sn.e: She takes the cup out of my hand and laughs.

sn.s: Me dice que medir es de gente que no sabe.
sn.e: She tells me measuring is for people who do not know.

sn.s: Después me enseña cómo se hace sin medir.
sn.e: Then she teaches me how it is done without measuring.

sn.s: Se agarra la sal con tres dedos y se tira.
sn.e: You take the salt with three fingers and throw it in.

sn.s: Se prueba, y si falta se le pone más.
sn.e: You taste it, and if it needs more you put more in.

sn.s: Se le pone poco a poco, nunca todo de una vez.
sn.e: You put it in little by little, never all at once.

sn.s: Porque sacarle sal a una olla no se puede.
sn.e: Because taking salt out of a pot cannot be done.

sn.s: Esa frase la repite tres veces en la mañana.
sn.e: She repeats that sentence three times in the morning.

sn.s: Se le pone y se deja: así habla ella de cocinar.
sn.e: You put it in and you leave it: that is how she talks about cooking.

sn.s: Se le pone el achiote, se deja media hora.
sn.e: You put in the achiote, you leave it half an hour.

sn.s: Se le pone la naranja agria, se deja otra vez.
sn.e: You put in the sour orange, you leave it again.

sn.s: Nunca dice yo pongo, siempre dice se le pone.
sn.e: She never says I put, she always says one puts.

sn.s: Como si la comida se hiciera sola y ella mirara.
sn.e: As if the food made itself and she just watched.

sn.s: Después hablamos de la sazón, que es la palabra grande.
sn.e: Then we talk about sazón, which is the big word.

sn.s: La sazón no es la receta ni los ingredientes.
sn.e: Sazón is not the recipe or the ingredients.

sn.s: La sazón es la mano de la persona que cocina.
sn.e: Sazón is the hand of the person cooking.

sn.s: Dos mujeres con la misma olla no sacan lo mismo.
sn.e: Two women with the same pot do not get the same thing.

sn.s: Una tiene sazón y la otra no, y así es.
sn.e: One has sazón and the other does not, and that is that.

sn.s: Le pregunto si la sazón se aprende.
sn.e: I ask her if sazón can be learned.

sn.s: Me dice que se agarra, que no es lo mismo.
sn.e: She tells me it is picked up, which is not the same.

sn.s: Se agarra viendo a alguien cocinar veinte años.
sn.e: It is picked up watching somebody cook for twenty years.

sn.s: Ella lo agarró viendo a su papá, no a su mamá.
sn.e: She picked it up watching her father, not her mother.

sn.s: A las once el agua de la olla empieza a hervir.
sn.e: At eleven the water in the pot starts to boil.

sn.s: Cuando hierve, ya no se abre la olla por nada.
sn.e: Once it boils, the pot is not opened for anything.

sn.s: El agua hierve abajo y la comida se cocina arriba.
sn.e: The water boils underneath and the food cooks on top.

sn.s: Si el agua no hierve parejo, la yuca queda dura.
sn.e: If the water does not boil evenly, the yuca stays hard.

sn.s: Ella sabe que hierve por el ruido, no por la tapa.
sn.e: She knows it is boiling by the sound, not by the lid.

sn.s: Si uno la abre, se le va el vapor y se arruina.
sn.e: If you open it, the steam goes and it is ruined.

sn.s: Doña Elena se sienta al lado de la olla a esperar.
sn.e: Doña Elena sits beside the pot to wait.

sn.s: Sabe que está listo por el olor, no por la hora.
sn.e: She knows it is ready by the smell, not by the clock.

sn.s: A la una destapa la olla y sale una nube de vapor.
sn.e: At one she uncovers the pot and a cloud of steam comes out.

sn.s: Chocho, dice Julio, que llegó por el olor.
sn.e: Chocho, says Julio, who came because of the smell.

sn.s: El baho se sirve con repollo curtido encima.
sn.e: The baho is served with pickled cabbage on top.

sn.s: Comemos catorce personas de una sola olla.
sn.e: Fourteen of us eat from one single pot.

sn.s: Yo trato de apuntar la receta esa noche en el cuarto.
sn.e: I try to write down the recipe that night in the bedroom.

sn.s: Escribo: yuca, plátano, carne, sal, achiote, naranja agria.
sn.e: I write: yuca, plantain, meat, salt, achiote, sour orange.

sn.s: Al lado de cada cosa escribo la cantidad que vi.
sn.e: Beside each thing I write the amount I saw.

sn.s: Y al lado de cada cantidad escribo un signo de pregunta.
sn.e: And beside each amount I write a question mark.

sn.s: La receta que escribí no le sirve a nadie.
sn.e: The recipe I wrote is no use to anybody.

sn.s: Lucía la lee y se ríe de mí toda la noche.
sn.e: Lucía reads it and laughs at me all night.

sn.s: Me dice que si quiero aprender, vaya los domingos.
sn.e: She tells me that if I want to learn, to go on Sundays.

sn.s: Veinte domingos y no un papel, dice ella.
sn.e: Twenty Sundays and not a piece of paper, she says.
